nonblocking: Fail-closed consequences of the strict gate, all STALE and never FRESH. (a) An isoformat() with a sub-minute UTC offset (+hh:mm:ss, which no current zone uses). (b) Hand-written contract-valid forms such as a space or lowercase 't' separator, '+0000', or hour-only times. (c) Any non-strict form, even before its expiry instant. The assembler and the RIG producer emit isoformat(), which matches the pattern.

The strict pattern checks shape only. Strings that match it but are calendar-invalid (e.g. 2026-02-30, 24:00) are rejected by contract.parse_ts and web_mvp.validate_bundle, so they can only reach the page through a hand-placed data.json. V8 rolls such a date forward to a later instant. This is outside the Python-accepted set the acceptance criterion covers.

Fuzz harness precision: Python instants beyond 2^53 microseconds (about year 2255) lose precision as JS numbers. The harness therefore uses exact floor_ms/rem_us, which removes the reviewer's 9999-12-31T23:59:59.999999 'rounding artifact'. My counts for the old app.js on the product set (64/188/14/33) differ slightly from the reviewer's (62/185/12/31). The causes are the exact-ceil instant and 3 duplicated hand forms.

nonblocking: N1 (display shape): metaToken() uses !/\s/, and JS \s does not match U+200B. A methodology id 'M_ZWSP​PROBE' is therefore displayed (escaped) as 'M_ZWSP​PROBE / TEST_VECTOR_V1'. The value is contract-valid and HTML-safe, so the only risk is an invisible character inside a displayed token (cosmetic or spoofing). NBSP, U+3000, tab, U+2028, empty and 65-character values are all correctly omitted.

N2 (fail-closed, not a violation): parse_ts accepts strict-shaped offsets with minutes 60-99. For example '2026-01-03T00:00+18:91' is read by Python as +19:31. These pass EXPIRES_AT, but Chromium's Date.parse returns NaN, so the page shows STALE even before expiry. There were 3,984 such forms in my corpus. Producers never emit them, because isoformat() always writes minutes below 60.

N3 (fail-closed, not a violation): when expires_at has sub-millisecond digits, Date.parse truncates to the millisecond, so the page shows STALE during the last <1 ms before Python's expiry. In the valid-producer set, all 65,783 sub-ms forms were STALE at T0-1ms and all were FRESH at T0-1s.

N4 (information only, not B1): 448 of the 59,026 strict-shaped strings that parse_ts REJECTS are still parsed by Date.parse. These are year 0000 and day overflow, e.g. '2000-11-31T20:49Z' is read as Dec 1. With a persisted FRESH, the page would show FRESH until that JS instant. No Python expiry exists for these strings, and web_mvp.validate_bundle rejects such bundles (ValueError 'day is out of range for month' / 'year 0 is out of range'). They are reachable only by hand-editing the served data.json.

N5 (by design, documented in the app.js comment): sub-minute UTC offsets ('+hh:mm:ss', which isoformat() emits for historical LMT zones) fail the gate and are always STALE. My valid-producer set excluded them on purpose.
